card.title: Find meaningful growth movement
card.what_to_watch: Scan the full dashboard and identify meaningful changes to qualified growth, then explain which connected signals matter for the operating decision.
card.why_watch: Growth leadership should hear about a broad change in qualified growth, not every noisy chart movement.
watch_for: A meaningful movement in qualified growth is identified.
The evidence distinguishes a broad growth problem from a local or expected change.
The result names the strongest related signals without claiming unsupported causation.
questions: Which charts show the meaningful change?
What related evidence best explains why it matters?
card.decision_guidance: Ignore normal or isolated movement. Investigate when qualified growth is materially off course and the evidence is ambiguous. Notify growth leadership when the movement is broad and corroborated.

card.title: Find customer-impacting delivery risk
card.what_to_watch: Scan all delivery charts and identify whether the customer-facing delivery promise is materially off course.
card.why_watch: Operations should act on broad service risk supported by warehouse, carrier, or inventory evidence rather than isolated late orders.
watch_for: Customer-facing delivery reliability is materially worse than baseline.
At least one operational signal corroborates or explains the movement.
Data freshness is sufficient for an operating decision.
questions: Is the delivery problem broad enough to act on?
Which connected operational signal should be investigated first?
card.decision_guidance: Ignore isolated order noise. Investigate ambiguous movement. Notify operations when delivery reliability is materially off course and supported by connected evidence.

card.title: Separate rollout effects from adoption risk
card.what_to_watch: Scan the dashboard for adoption changes that are meaningfully off the planned rollout path.
card.why_watch: Product leadership needs to avoid escalating planned cohort and release effects as product failures.
watch_for: Adoption is materially different from the expected rollout path.
Release and experiment context distinguishes planned movement from a real adoption problem.
Instrumentation quality is sufficient before action.
questions: Is the movement an adoption problem or an expected rollout effect?
What evidence should product inspect next?
card.decision_guidance: Ignore movement explained by the planned rollout calendar or expected cohort mix. Investigate only contradictory or unsupported adoption movement.

card.title: Detect payment risk without trusting broken data
card.what_to_watch: Scan payment, issuer, fraud, and control charts for a meaningful customer or risk movement.
card.why_watch: Payments leadership needs a trustworthy signal before intervening in revenue or risk controls.
watch_for: Payment completion or loss changes materially across the customer population.
Issuer or fraud evidence helps distinguish a recoverable issue from a risk event.
Freshness and comparability are sufficient before automatic delivery.
questions: Is this a payment problem or a data trust problem?
Which connected evidence should the payments team inspect?
card.decision_guidance: Escalate a severe payment trust failure. Do not notify on a large movement when the source is stale, incomplete, or not comparable.

card.title: Find customer-impacting reliability incidents
card.what_to_watch: Scan the platform dashboard and identify whether a customer-impacting reliability change needs escalation.
card.why_watch: Platform leaders should receive a concise incident signal with the relevant service, deploy, and capacity evidence.
watch_for: Customer error rate or latency is materially worse than the operating baseline.
A deploy, incident, or capacity signal forms a coherent explanation.
The signal is severe enough to require platform leadership attention.
questions: Which operational evidence best explains the change?
card.decision_guidance: Escalate only when customer impact is corroborated by operational evidence. Ignore isolated host noise.

card.title: Do not alert on normal dashboard noise
card.what_to_watch: Scan the complete dashboard and identify only changes that are meaningful for the stated operating objective.
card.why_watch: Leadership attention is scarce and normal chart variation should not create a notification.
watch_for: A movement is materially outside the normal operating pattern.
The evidence is sufficient to distinguish signal from ordinary noise.
questions: If not, should this run produce no delivery?
card.decision_guidance: Ignore ordinary variation, small movements, and isolated charts. Notify only when a material movement is corroborated by related evidence.
